about: Lays an application out: bars across the top and the bottom, as many as it renders, and a body between them with panels on either side of the page, as many as it renders. Each panel states its width, how it closes and when it folds, and the root states what scrolls and which look. A shell reads on a phone without being told: the navbar folds below the `md` breakpoint and the aside below `lg`. Eleven applications here, each laid out on the one shell.

billing.about: Bars stack in the order they render, each as tall as its content: a notice above the toolbar.
billing.title: A billing console, a notice above the toolbar

brokeOne: Retries broke first. A slow partner bank made each worker retry the same payout, and the queue grew faster than we drained it.
brokeTwo: Idempotency keys stopped the duplicate payments, but the delays remained. We moved each partner to a queue of its own.
canary: Canary looks clean, error rate flat.

canvas.about: The floating look raises each panel's content as a card with a margin around it, and the canvas runs behind. The layers close from the menu button and the properties from Details.
canvas.title: A design tool, panels afloat

chat.about: Panels render across in order, each with its own width and named for its triggers. The rail of workspaces never folds. The panel of channels beside it closes from the menu button and folds below the `md` breakpoint, as a navbar does by default.
chat.title: A chat client, a rail beside the channels

checkout.about: A header and the page alone. A part that is not rendered takes no room, so a checkout states nothing about the navigation it does not have.
checkout.title: A checkout, header and page alone

console.about: A toolbar, a sidebar of pages with a search, the page, an aside and a footer. The menu button, the rail on the navbar's edge and ⌘B close the navbar to icons, and the sidebar follows. Details closes the aside. The navbar leaves the body below the `sm` breakpoint here and the aside below `lg`, and each opens over the page from its control.
console.title: An operations console

handbook.about: A bar renders where it is placed: in the main region it spans the page alone, and the navbar runs the full height beside it. Both bars here are pinned, the toolbar to the top of the page and the footer to its bottom, and the page scrolls between them. The inset look raises the page as a card on a muted ground.
handbook.title: A handbook, sidebar first and page inset

heroBody: Ledger runs your releases, checks every deploy and rolls back when an error rate climbs.
hoursOne: Core hours run from 10:00 to 16:00 in your own time zone. Outside them, plan your day around your work and your life.
hoursTwo: Put leave and appointments in the team calendar, so nobody waits on you for an answer.
invoiceBody: Hi, the invoice from March has not been settled. Could you have a look?
invoicesAppear: Invoices appear here when your first billing period closes.

journal.about: While the window scrolls, a panel sticks under the pinned bars and is as tall as the room they leave, so the contents reach the bottom of the window however far the article has scrolled.
journal.title: A journal, the contents stuck under the masthead

keptOne: We kept the ledger. Every payout is still written once, and every retry reads it before it sends anything.
keptTwo: We also kept the alerts. They fire on the age of the oldest message, which is what a customer notices.

mail.about: The folders close to icons: the track moves to the rail's width and remains in reach, and the sidebar inside it renders its rows as icons. Press the menu button or the rail on its edge to see the track move. The list beside it is a second panel, and the message is the page.
mail.title: A mail client, folders closing to icons

meetingsOne: Every meeting has an agenda in its invite and ends five minutes early. A meeting without an agenda is cancelled.
meetingsTwo: Decisions are made in the document, not in the call. The call is for the questions the document leaves open.
movedOne: For three years every payout went through one queue. It was simple to run and easy to reason about, until the day it was neither.
movedQuote: A queue hides its backlog until the backlog is the problem.
movedTwo: We replaced it with one queue per partner bank, so a slow partner delays only its own payouts.
nextOne: Next we move refunds onto the same design, and add a dashboard with the age of every queue.
nextTwo: If you run a service that sends money, the runbook for the new queues is in the handbook under On call.

player.about: A footer told to stick pins to the bottom of the window while the page scrolls, so the player remains in reach however far the library has scrolled.
player.title: A music player, the player pinned to the bottom

reader.about: Two columns and no navbar: the article is the page, and the notes that go with it are an aside told to fold under. Below the `lg` breakpoint the aside drops under the article as a block, the way related notes read on a phone, and its trigger renders nothing, because there is nothing to open.
reader.title: A reader, the page and a column beside it

storefront.about: Told that the window scrolls, the root grows with the page and the window scrolls. A bar told to stick pins to the top while the page scrolls by. Here the window is a box of a stated height.
storefront.title: A storefront, the toolbar pinned

teapotAbout: Brews four cups, with a steel strainer
title: App shell
update: Last updated 3 days ago by Mara
whyMoved: Why we moved off the queue
workingHereAbout: How we plan the week, when we meet, and how decisions are written down.
writingOne: Write a proposal before you build anything that takes more than a week. Keep it to one page, with the problem first.
writingTwo: Link the proposal from the ticket, so the next person finds the reasoning without asking.
